heard: A massive asteroid once reached the highest hazard rating in history. Discovered in 2004, asteroid Apophis was given a 2.7% chance of slamming into Earth. But radar observations in March 2021 definitively ruled out any collision for at least a century. Yet on Friday, April 13, 2029, the 450-meter rock will still make history. It will sweep less than 32,000 kilometers above us, passing closer than our geostationary satellites. Billions of people in Europe, Africa, and Asia can watch it with the naked eye. During this flyby, Earth's gravitational tidal forces will twist the asteroid and trigger surface movements. This intense cosmic encounter will forever alter the orbit of the massive asteroid.
